transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, my job sent me. 

I guess I've just been... forgetting things lately. Like scheduled callbacks, or... work orders. Just basic follow-ups I promised people I'd do. It kind of piled up on me, and... they told me I needed to come see someone before I lose my shot at moving up. So... that's why I'm here.
Have you struggled with this kind of forgetfulness and difficulty keeping track of tasks since you were a child, or is this something that has only started happening more recently?

Um... no, it's not new. It's... always been like this, really. Back in grade school, long before any of this pressure at work. 

I guess... teachers used to say I was bright, but I was always misplacing my papers. Or I'd miss parts of the directions they gave us. They always had to remind me to just... finish my classwork. So, yeah. It's been happening since I was a kid.
When you were in school, did you find it difficult to stay seated or feel like you constantly needed to be moving around?
Um... no. Not really. I didn't have trouble staying in my seat or anything. I was mostly just... quiet, I guess.
Aside from the forgetfulness, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or uninterested in things you usually enjoy?
Um... no. Not really. I'm not... sad or anything. I still like doing my regular stuff. It's just... the work things I keep messing up. But no.
Do you often find yourself acting or speaking without thinking about the consequences first?
Um... no. I don't think so. I usually... keep to myself. I don't really do things like that.
When you have to work on a task that you find boring or uninteresting, do you find it difficult to keep your attention on it until it is finished?

Yeah... I guess. Like with the digital work orders I have to do. I'll start reading the notes, thinking I've got it, but... halfway through, my mind just slips off. I'll hear a noise or think about the next job, and... I just realize I don't even know what I just looked at. So... yeah.
